author: David Hinojosa
title: Nick Rogers resigns after five seasons as Pieper head football coach - NewsBreak
text:
By David Hinojosa ,
9 hours ago Pieper head coach Nick Rogers talks to his team after a 28-14 loss to Liberty Hill in the Class 5A Division II state quarterfinals on Friday, Dec. 1, 2023, in San Marcos, Texas. Rogers has resigned as the Warriors' head football coach, he confirmed to the Express-News on Wednesday. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) Pieper football coach Nick Rogers is stepping down after leading the Warriors during the program's first five seasons, he confirmed to the Express-News on Wednesday.
Rogers compiled a 33-24 record in four varsity seasons, which included three playoff appearances and a trip to the state quarterfinals in 2023 in the program’s second year of varsity. The Warriors were 8-5 and advanced to the third round of the playoffs in 2025.
“I am taking some time to focus more on my family,” Rogers said in a text.
Rogers opened the Pieper program in 2021 and played a sub-varsity schedule for one season. He previously was the offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach for five years at Cedar Park.
Pieper principal Lauran Knight released a letter to parents regarding the news.
“While this is certainly a significant change for our school community, we respect and support his decision to pursue opportunities outside of education,” Knight wrote. “We sincerely thank Coach Rogers for his dedication and service to Pieper High School over the past five years. We are grateful for his leadership, and more importantly for the positive impact he has made on our students. We wish him the very best in his future endeavors.”
Knight said the search for his replacement has started.
